crm_notes: POC focused on latency SLO definition and measurement alignment. Customer cares about client-observed end-to-end latency for their agents, but also needs guaranteed server-side processing SLOs for contractual SLAs. They repeatedly asked: 'How do you measure p99 — is it on the client or server? Are streaming tokens counted per-chunk or end-to-end?'
latency_slo_summary: Customer requires two SLO layers: 1) End-to-end client SLOs (p50/p95/p99) measured from agent desktop, target examples: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms for non-streaming / full-response; streaming: per-chunk p95 < 80ms, end-to-end time-to-first-token p95 < 120ms. 2) Server-side SLI for Redwood runtime: inference-only processing time (model forward + batching overhead) p50/p95/p99 targets set tighter to allow network/postprocessing budgets. Agreement: define both SLIs and clear mapping/attribution so legal can write SLA credits.
measurement_plan: Agree dual-instrumentation: client RUM (browser/agent SDK) for end-to-end numbers + server-side tracing and log SLI for model-processing times. Explicitly store both timings on each request: client_start, client_first_byte, server_received, model_start, model_end, server_sent. Compute p50/p95/p99 over rolling 1-minute windows and daily aggregates; alert on 5-min sustained breach. Use separate metrics for streaming (per-chunk latency and TTFB) vs non-streaming (full response latency).
slo_definition_details: - Non-streaming SLOs defined on end-to-end request-complete latency. Example targets: p50 50-60ms, p95 120-150ms, p99 300-350ms (depends on model size).
streaming_vs_non_streaming_notes: Streaming: agreed to measure both TTFB (time-to-first-token) and per-chunk append latency. Should report p50/p95 for chunk latency and TTFB separately. For long responses, put SLOs on percent of chunks meeting threshold (e.g., 99% of chunks p95 < 120ms) rather than total response time. Client-side buffering and websocket jitter to be accounted for in client SLI.
client_vs_server_timing_notes: Customer wants both client-observed and server-processed SLIs. Legal wants contractual SLOs on client-observed numbers but will accept a server-side SLA if we provide attribution rules that exclude client-network incidents. Proposal: contractual SLOs: end-to-end p95 150ms with a transparent exception policy (DNS, CDN issues, customer network). Server-side SLOs used for internal fallbacks and remediation SLAs.
poC_scope_and_metrics: 3-week dedicated POC: provision 2 reserved GPU instances (N model family), run their agent traffic replay (60k req/day), measure p50/p95/p99 for both streaming and non-streaming routes, validate autoscaling behavior under concurrency, produce a final SLO alignment doc and recommended reserved GPU sizing. Deliverables: SLO mapping spreadsheet, synthetic vs production delta analysis, recommendation for reserved pool sizing and burst policies.
sla_negotiation_points: Customer requests: monthly uptime + latency SLA. Proposed: 99.9% availability for reserved pool; latency credit if monthly p95 breach exceeds 0.5% of requests. Need legal to sign off on exception carve-outs and measurement authority (Redwood metrics vs customer RUM).
